# ForkMesh

> ForkMesh is an open-source developer platform for publishing, browsing, mirroring, discussing and shipping software across independent hosts, so no single hosting provider owns a project. Git stays the source of truth, any node can mirror a public repository, and issues, pull requests, reviews and releases are signed records stored in the repository.

- Git repository bytes live on developer-operated hosts and server mirrors. Clones are served from a live, signed, integrity-checked mirror, so a repository stays reachable when its source host goes offline.
- Public repositories can be read and cloned with stock Git and no account: `git clone https://forkmesh.com/<owner>/<repo>`. ForkMesh's own source is `https://forkmesh.com/forkmesh/forkmesh`.
- Collaboration records (issues, discussions, pull requests, reviews, projects, milestones, releases) live under `.forkmesh/` in the repository and are signed with each node's Ed25519 identity.
- The desktop app (Qt, Linux, macOS, Windows) is a full node: it hosts and mirrors repositories, and runs Codex or Claude Code agents in isolated worktrees whose work becomes pull requests. The iPhone and Android apps are access clients.
- The protocol, self-hosting, public read and clone, and portable Git data are free; only bounded hosted services are paid.
- Hosts: forkmesh.com is the website and docs, app.forkmesh.com is the web app and HTTP API, world.forkmesh.com is the 3D ForkMesh World.
- Install the desktop node on Linux or macOS: `curl -fsSL https://forkmesh.com/install.sh | bash`

## Docs

- [Documentation overview](https://forkmesh.com/docs/): install, quickstart, the ForkMesh mental model, APIs and self-hosting
- [Getting started](https://forkmesh.com/docs/getting-started/): first run, creating or adding a repository, chat and a first change
- [Reading and cloning without an account](https://forkmesh.com/docs/accountless-reading/): what anonymous visitors and stock Git can do
- [Stock Git compatibility](https://forkmesh.com/docs/git-compatibility/): supported clone, fetch, push, partial-clone, bundle, submodule and signed-commit workflows
- [Repositories created on the web](https://forkmesh.com/docs/hosted-repositories/): push over HTTPS to a hosted repository
- [Repository imports](https://forkmesh.com/docs/repository-imports/): bring a repository from another forge, with resumable migration
- [Two-way forge sync](https://forkmesh.com/docs/forge-sync/): keep issues and comments in step with GitHub, Gitea or Forgejo
- [Product promise proof](https://forkmesh.com/docs/product-promise/): collaborate, add a mirror, take the source offline and clone again
- [Desktop client](https://forkmesh.com/docs/qt-client/): the Qt desktop application
- [Team onboarding](https://forkmesh.com/docs/onboarding/): bring a team onto ForkMesh
- [Terminology](https://forkmesh.com/docs/terminology/): the Git words ForkMesh keeps and the network ideas it adds, such as mirrors and seeding

## API and integrations

- [Integration contract (v1)](https://forkmesh.com/docs/integrations/): the stable HTTP resources, authentication, webhooks, signatures and pagination
- [OpenAPI description](https://app.forkmesh.com/api/openapi.json): every route the app serves; only the integration contract routes are stable
- [Service status](https://app.forkmesh.com/api/status): machine-readable status of each system

## Protocol

- [Protocol spec](https://forkmesh.com/docs/protocol/): signed collaboration objects, routing and the wire format
- [Signatures and authentication](https://forkmesh.com/docs/protocol/signatures-and-authentication/): how records and requests are signed and verified
- [Threat model](https://forkmesh.com/docs/protocol/threat-model/): what the protocol defends against
- [Portable identities and recovery](https://forkmesh.com/docs/portable-identities/): node keys, accounts and recovery
- [Transports and anonymity postures](https://forkmesh.com/docs/transports/): the network paths a node can use
- [Offline and low-bandwidth sync](https://forkmesh.com/docs/offline-sync/): bundles, removable media and slow links

## Product

- [Features](https://forkmesh.com/features): everything the mesh can do
- [Desktop downloads](https://forkmesh.com/desktop): native packages from the signed release manifest
- [Mobile](https://forkmesh.com/mobile): agents, Git and code review on iPhone and iPad
- [Market](https://forkmesh.com/market): extensions, agents, themes and virtual goods
- [When ForkMesh fits, and when it does not](https://forkmesh.com/docs/category-comparisons/): comparison with other forges
- [Free protocol, paid services](https://forkmesh.com/docs/business-model/): what is always free and what is paid
- [Changelog](https://forkmesh.com/changelog): released changes
- [Blog](https://forkmesh.com/blog): product announcements

## Optional

- [Documentation library](https://forkmesh.com/docs/library/): every guide, design note, runbook and schema
- [Capability matrix](https://forkmesh.com/docs/capability-matrix/): which surface (desktop, web, mobile, headless) supports what
- [Installation support matrix](https://forkmesh.com/docs/install-support-matrix/): installable builds, how they are verified, and upgrade, rollback and uninstall
- [Running a mirror node](https://forkmesh.com/docs/operations/mirror-node/): operate a headless server mirror
- [Private repository confidentiality](https://forkmesh.com/docs/security/private-repository-confidentiality/): how private repositories are protected
- [About](https://forkmesh.com/about): the team and the project
- [Report a vulnerability](https://forkmesh.com/security-report): private security disclosure
- [ForkMesh World](https://world.forkmesh.com/): a 3D view of repositories, nodes, agents and activity
